description:
Five sibling MemoryBackends have:

  crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/memory.rs:799
  crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:540
  crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:718
  crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:529
  crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/memory.rs:723

    fn json_merge_patch(target: &mut serde_json::Value, patch: serde_json::Value) {
        match patch {
            serde_json::Value::Object(patch_map) => {
                let target_map = target
                    .as_object_mut()
                    .expect("merge patch target must be an object");
                ...

This .expect() fires whenever the caller-supplied target is not a JSON Object — e.g. if a future code path passes in a JSON Value::Number or Value::Array. Currently impossible because callers always serialize a SetObject (which serializes to an Object), but the function is private and the invariant is implicit, not type-enforced.

Per AGENTS.md error-handling rule: '.unwrap() or .expect() outside of tests, examples, or provably unreachable paths. Every one in production code needs a comment explaining why it cannot fail.' The comment here is the panic-message string itself, which states the invariant but doesn't explain WHY it holds (i.e. that all call sites guarantee Object inputs).

Why P3 not P2: feature-gated behind 'memory'; private function; reachable only via the module's own create_object/update_object which both pass typed-serialized objects. The panic is well-bounded.

Two acceptable fixes:
1. Change fn signature: fn json_merge_patch(target: &mut serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>, patch: serde_json::Value) — bake the invariant into the type. Callers do .as_object_mut() once at the entry point.
2. Add a //   SAFETY-style comment before the .expect() explaining why every call site is statically guaranteed to pass a Value::Object.

Canonical mail-server does NOT have json_merge_patch in this shape — it merges via a different path (search for 'merge_patch' in crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs returns no matches), so the 5 siblings introduced this independently. Cookie-cutter divergence as well as the error-handling smell.
title: P3: json_merge_patch panics via expect('merge patch target must be an object') in 5 sibling MemoryBackends — internal data path, but unreachable on success
